analysis.executiveSummary:
This coverage-gap deep dive into Oddzilla's settlement internals, wallet-watcher reorg/discovery path, and the (currently dormant) BetBuilder/OBB subsystem surfaced 7 confirmed findings, including 1 critical and 3 high. The dominant theme is decoupling: state that is priced/validated in one place but settled from another. The BetBuilder critical (OBB-validated selectionIds never bound to the persisted ticket_selections that actually decide win/loss) and the BetBuilder cashout mispricing both let a bettor's payout be driven by client-controlled per-leg data that the OBB session never sanctioned. The settlement-correctness high (cancel-after-settle skipping an already-resolved leg on an 'accepted' multibet) is the headline real-money bug in code that ships today — it pays winnings on a market Oddin officially cancelled, and is reachable on any combo straddling a per-map market that Oddin settles then cancels.

The wallet-watcher findings cluster around a fragile discovery contract: a transient per-row INSERT error advances the scan cursor anyway (high — a USDC deposit is lost forever with no alert), and the deposit_intents unique key omits log_index, silently dropping a second USDC Transfer in one tx (low). Both stem from treating best-effort per-row failures as benign while the cursor marches forward monotonically. A low-severity ledger-audit issue (re-settle generation ref_id collides across payout/refund types) does not move money but breaks the 1:1 credit↔adjustment reconciliation invariant. A medium availability hole (OBB SessionInfo has no gRPC deadline and is awaited inside the placement transaction holding FOR UPDATE row locks) becomes live the moment ODDIN_OBB_HOST is set.

Headline risk and timing: the cancel-after-settle combo mispay and the two wallet-watcher deposit-loss bugs affect production today and warrant immediate fixes plus regression tests. The three BetBuilder findings (critical + high + medium) are gated off in prod (ODDIN_OBB_HOST empty) but MUST be fixed before OBB is enabled — the critical is a systematic +EV drain, not an edge case. Cross-cutting weakness: no test exercises the accepted-multibet cancel path, the OBB selectionId↔selections binding, or wallet-watcher cursor-on-error behavior.
topPriorities: Fix cancel-after-settle: void/clear an already-resolved leg on an 'accepted' multibet (drop the AND result IS NULL guard or call ReverseSelectionsForTicketOnMarket unconditionally) — ships in prod, real fund loss
Make wallet-watcher per-row INSERT errors fatal to the tick (return err, gate BumpCursor on no row error) — transient DB blip = permanently lost USDC deposit
Before enabling OBB: bind OBB selectionIds to req.selections — reconstruct canonical ids server-side and assert set-equality, else bettor settles a different leg set than was priced
Before enabling OBB: block betbuilder in the cashout engine (add to bet_type_unsupported) — non-multiplicative odds + client-controlled per-leg odds = near-full-payout cashout drain
Add log_index to deposit_intents unique key (migration) so a second USDC Transfer in one tx is credited or alerted, not silently dropped
Wire a hard per-call gRPC deadline on OBB SessionInfo and move it OUTSIDE the placement tx so a hung Oddin can't hold FOR UPDATE locks
Make re-settle generation ref_id monotonic across payout+refund types so every credit keeps a 1:1 adjustment row for reconciliation
Add regression tests for: accepted-combo cancel void, OBB id binding, and wallet-watcher cursor-on-insert-error
coverageGaps: Tiple/Tippot cancel-after-settle: the confirmed combo bug names tiple/tippot/betbuilder as affected, but per-product void/refund semantics under a cancelled resolved leg were not independently traced for tiple (anyWin) and tippot (tier ladder) — verify each product's recompute after the void fix

Specifier-hash byte-identity across the TS + two Go implementations was named in scope but not re-verified against docs/fixtures/specifiers.json in this pass — confirm the golden table still passes in all three

Settlement under concurrent workers: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED interaction between applyMarketSettle and applyMarketCancel on the same multibet across two AMQP messages was not exercised — check whether a SKIP-LOCKED miss during cancel can leave a leg permanently unvoided
Reorg handling for the second USDC Transfer / unattributed path: whether VerifyDeposit + block_hash reorg flip interacts correctly with the log_index-less dedup
OBB session replay: whether the same sessionId can be reused across two POST /bets to double-place at one validated price was not assessed

Cashout drift/saturation for legitimate combos (non-betbuilder) under attacker-influenced oddsAtPlacement was only assessed transitively via the betbuilder path — confirm combo placement still hard-validates per-leg drift so the cashout cap can't be gamed there
rankedTitles: BetBuilder: OBB-validated selectionIds are never bound to the persisted ticket_selections that drive settlement — placement can settle a different leg set than was priced
Cancel-after-settle does not void an already-resolved combo leg when the ticket is still pending (combo mispay / fund loss)
Per-row insert error during discovery advances the cursor anyway — USDC deposit silently lost forever
BetBuilder tickets are cashable through the simple-cashout engine, which mis-prices them and lets a bettor control the cashout value via arbitrary per-leg odds
obb-client never sets a gRPC deadline; a hung SessionInfo holds the bet-placement transaction (and its row locks) open inside POST /bets
deposit_intents unique key omits log_index — second USDC Transfer in one tx is silently dropped
Re-settle generation ref_id collides across bet_payout/bet_refund types, dropping the compensating adjustment ledger row on alternating-result rollbacks

findings.title: Cancel-after-settle does not void an already-resolved combo leg when the ticket is still pending (combo mispay / fund loss)
findings.description: In applyCancelToTickets the per-ticket void path only clears a selection's prior result (ReverseSelectionsForTicketOnMarket, which sets result=NULL unconditionally) when the ticket was previously 'settled' (reversed==true). For a multi-leg ticket (combo/tiple/tippot/betbuilder) that is still in status 'accepted' because other legs are unresolved, but which already has a RESOLVED leg on the now-cancelled market (Oddin can settle a per-map market, then cancel it — cancel-after-settle is an explicitly handled sequence), reverseSettledForCancel returns reversed=false (the ticket is 'accepted', not 'settled'). ReverseSelectionsForTicketOnMarket is therefore skipped, and VoidSelectionsForTicketOnMarket runs with its `AND result IS NULL` filter (settler/store.go:352), which skips the already-resolved leg. The leg keeps its stale result (e.g. 'won'/'lost') instead of being voided. When the remaining legs later resolve and the ticket settles, computePayout/ComboPayout reads ticket_selections.result directly and multiplies in the cancelled leg's odds (won) or zeroes the ticket (lost). A leg whose market Oddin officially cancelled is thus paid as if it won — over-paying the bettor and creating real fund loss for the operator. (Singles are unaffected: a single settles the instant its one leg resolves, so it is never 'accepted' with a resolved leg; the cancel-after-settle reverse-then-void path handles it correctly.)
findings.exploitScenario: Bettor places a 2-leg combo: leg A = Map 1 winner on match X, leg B = Map 2 winner on match X (or a leg on another match). Oddin settles Map 1: leg A resolves 'won', combo ticket stays 'accepted' (leg B pending). Oddin then issues bet_cancel for the Map 1 market (e.g. void_reason 'not played'/'suspended' after a remap). applyMarketCancel flips the market to -4 and calls applyCancelToTickets; the ticket is 'accepted' so reversed=false, leg A's result='won' is not cleared, and VoidSelectionsForTicketOnMarket skips it (result not NULL). Leg B later resolves 'won'. The combo settles paying stake × oddsA × oddsB even though leg A's market was cancelled — the operator pays winnings on a voided market. Repeatable on any combo straddling a per-map market that Oddin settles then cancels.
findings.recommendation: Void the cancelled-market legs regardless of ticket-settled state. Either (a) call ReverseSelectionsForTicketOnMarket unconditionally (not only when reversed==true) before VoidSelectionsForTicketOnMarket so the leg is cleared to NULL then voided, or (b) drop the `AND result IS NULL` guard from VoidSelectionsForTicketOnMarket so a bet_cancel forcibly overwrites any prior per-leg result with void (cancel semantically supersedes a prior settle on that market). Add a test for: combo with one already-resolved leg on the cancelled market while another leg is unresolved, asserting the cancelled leg ends as 'void' and the combo refunds/recomputes accordingly.
findings.verifierEvidence:
services/settlement/internal/settler/settler.go:261 (ApplyOutcomeToSelections on all affected tickets); :556-577 (maybeSettleTicket leaves combo 'accepted' when UnresolvedCountIn>0); :825-839 (applyCancelToTickets: ReverseSelectionsForTicketOnMarket gated on reversed); :856-863 (reverseSettledForCancel false unless Status=='settled'); :733-806 (applyMarketCancel has no market-wide selection reset). services/settlement/internal/store/store.go:346-357 (VoidSelectionsForTicketOnMarket AND result IS NULL); :262-272 (ApplyOutcomeToSelections writes won/lost); :572-580 (UnresolvedCountIn counts only NULL). services/settlement/internal/settler/payout.go:45-84,115-151 (ComboPayout/EffectiveFactor read sel.Result directly, factor = full odds for 'won'). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:255-261 (cancel-after-settle design only covers fully-'settled' tickets). No *_test.go covers the per-ticket cancel-void path. | Traced the full chain end-to-end:

1. applyMarketSettle (settler.go:179-265) calls store.ApplyOutcomeToSelections (store.go:262-282) on a per-map bet_settlement. That UPDATE sets ticket_selections.result/void_factor for ALL tickets with a selection on that market, gated only by `WHERE market_id=$1 AND outcome_id=$2 AND result IS NULL` — it does NOT filter on the parent ticket's status. So a combo still in 'accepted' status gets its resolved leg's result set to e.g. 'won'.

2. maybeSettleTicket (settler.go:556-577) leaves the ticket in 'accepted' when UnresolvedCountIn(selections) > 0 (store.go:572-580 counts legs with empty result). So a 2-leg combo with one resolved leg + one pending leg stays 'accepted' carrying a non-NULL result on the settled leg. Confirmed mechanism for "accepted ticket with a resolved leg."

3. bet_cancel for that market: handleBetCancel → applyMarketCancel (settler.go:733-805). With end_time absent, deactivateMarket=true (status→-4) and applyCancelToTickets runs (settler.go:787, 814-849). AffectedTicketsForMarketInWindow (store.go:320-341) joins tickets WITHOUT a status filter, so the 'accepted' combo IS captured.

4. In the per-ticket loop, reverseSettledForCancel (settler.go:856-862) returns reversed=false unless t.Status=='settled'. The accepted combo is NOT 'settled', so reversed=false → ReverseSelectionsForTicketOnMarket (which would NULL the result, store.go:362-371) is SKIPPED (settler.go:832-836).

5. VoidSelectionsForTicketOnMarket (store.go:346-357) then runs with `WHERE ticket_id=$1 AND market_id=$2 AND result IS NULL` — the already-resolved leg has result='won' (not NULL), so it is SKIPPED. The leg keeps its stale 'won' result; its market is now -4 (sticky terminal, never reactivates).

6. When the remaining leg later resolves, maybeSettleTicket → ComboPayout (payout.go:115-151) reads sel.Result and sel.OddsAtPlacement directly and multiplies EffectiveFactor for the 'won' leg (eff=odds) into the product — paying stake × oddsA × oddsB even though leg A's market was officially cancelled. Same defect applies to TiplePayout (anyWin→full pay), TippotPayout (higher tier), and BetBuilderPayout (all-won) since all read sel.Result directly.

No compensating control neutralizes it: the apply-once 5-tuple/ledger index, advisory lock, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and sticky-status guard all protect different invariants and none clear/void a resolved leg on an accepted multibet during cancel. No test exercises the accepted-combo-with-resolved-leg cancel path (grep found references only in the two implementation files). CLAUDE.md itself documents cancel-after-settle as a real, handled Oddin sequence — the reverse-then-void logic was written for the single/settled case and silently misses the accepted-multibet case. | settler.go:825-839 (applyCancelToTickets: ReverseSelectionsForTicketOnMarket gated on reversed==true, then unconditional VoidSelectionsForTicketOnMarket); settler.go:856-863 (reverseSettledForCancel returns false for non-'settled' ticket); store.go:346-357 (VoidSelectionsForTicketOnMarket has AND result IS NULL); store.go:262-286 (ApplyOutcomeToSelections resolves a leg at market-settle time regardless of ticket status); settler.go:575-577 (maybeSettleTicket leaves combo 'accepted' while a leg is unresolved); payout.go:115-151 + payout.go:45-84 (ComboPayout/EffectiveFactor multiply the un-voided 'won' leg's full odds); settler.go:733-806 (applyMarketCancel calls only applyCancelToTickets, never the batch void); service.ts:456-465 (cross-match combos allowed → reachable cross-match exploit).

findings.title: Re-settle generation ref_id collides across bet_payout/bet_refund types, dropping the compensating adjustment ledger row on alternating-result rollbacks
findings.description: nextPayoutRefID counts existing ledger rows scoped by `type` (line 895: `AND type = $2`), so the generation suffix is incremented PER ledger type independently. A re-settle whose result type differs from a prior generation (e.g. gen1 = win → bet_payout ref_id=T; gen2 after rollback = all-void combo → bet_refund) gets ref_id=T again because no prior bet_refund row exists — valid, since the unique index is on (type, ref_type, ref_id). But on the NEXT rollback, ReverseSettledTicket calls LatestUnreversedPayoutRefID, which returns the newest bet_payout/bet_refund row lacking a matching `adjustment` row with the SAME ref_id (lines 927-932). Since the gen1 rollback already wrote an adjustment with ref_id=T, the gen2 bet_refund row (also ref_id=T) is treated as already-reversed (an adjustment with ref_id=T exists), so LatestUnreversedPayoutRefID returns not-found and the gen2 adjustment ledger row is skipped entirely. The wallet UPDATE in ReverseSettledTicket still runs (money stays correct), but the audit invariant the code documents ('every reversed credit has a matching adjustment', store.go:915-919) is silently violated. Reconciliation tools that pair each unreversed credit 1:1 with current ticket state will miscount.
findings.exploitScenario: Not directly exploitable for fund loss (wallet math is via unconditional UPDATE), but a market that Oddin settle→rollback→re-settle(as void)→rollback cycles produces a ledger where the second reversal has no adjustment row. An auditor reconciling wallet_ledger sums against ticket states sees an orphaned bet_refund credit with no compensating entry, masking or fabricating apparent drift during a financial review.
findings.recommendation: Make the generation suffix monotonic across ALL ledger types for a ticket, not per-type: count rows of type IN ('bet_payout','bet_refund') (matching LatestUnreversedPayoutRefID's scope) when computing the next suffix, so every generation — regardless of result type — gets a distinct ref_id (T, T:2, T:3, …). That keeps each payout/refund row 1:1 with its adjustment row. Add a settle→rollback→re-settle-as-void→rollback test asserting exactly one adjustment row per credit row.
findings.verifierEvidence: store.go:891-897 nextPayoutRefID COUNT scoped `AND type = $2::wallet_tx_type`; store.go:922-934 LatestUnreversedPayoutRefID matches adjustment by ref_id only (line 931, no type filter) over type IN ('bet_payout','bet_refund'); store.go:979-1000 ReverseSettledTicket skips adjustment insert when found=false while wallet UPDATE (970-977) is unconditional; settler.go:579-584 computePayout yields bet_payout|bet_refund passed to SettleTicket; store.go:700-704 INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (type,ref_type,ref_id) lets ('bet_refund','ticket','T') coexist with ('bet_payout','ticket','T'); store.go:635-657 RiskZilla reverse is ref_id-independent unconditional UPDATE.

findings.title: Per-row insert error during discovery advances the cursor anyway — USDC deposit silently lost forever
findings.description: DiscoverIncoming's design contract (its own doc comment, lines 187-189: "it only advances after both succeed, so a transient failure in either re-runs the same range next tick") is only honoured for failures of the eth_getLogs calls themselves. A failure of an individual row INSERT is NOT honoured. In Scan 1, when v.st.InsertDiscoveredIntent returns an error the loop logs a warning and `continue`s (lines 262-264); in Scan 2, when v.st.InsertUnattributedDeposit (or HasDepositIntentFor) errors the loop also `continue`s (lines 283-290, 305-308). After the loops, BumpCursor(toBlock) runs unconditionally (line 312). So a transient DB error (deadlock, connection blip, statement timeout, brief pool exhaustion) while inserting one Transfer permanently advances the scan cursor past that block. Because there is NO paste-hash route any more (wallet/routes.ts header comment lines 11-15) and the only insert path for a USDC credit is InsertDiscoveredIntent, a USDC transfer whose intent INSERT transiently failed is never retried: Scan 2 skips it (line 275 `continue` for the USDC contract) so it isn't even surfaced as an unattributed alert, and the cursor never returns to that block range (BumpCursor uses GREATEST, store.go:68). The user's funds reach the operator's receive address but are never credited and never flagged.
findings.exploitScenario: A whitelisted user sends 500 USDC. The discovery tick fetches the log, but at the exact moment InsertDiscoveredIntent runs Postgres returns a transient error (e.g. `40P01` deadlock with a concurrent credit tx touching deposit_intents, or a 1-second pool stall during a deploy). The loop logs `insert discovered intent` warn, continues, and BumpCursor advances to toBlock. The deposit is gone: no intent row, no unattributed row, no admin alert. The user files a support ticket; the operator must manually reconstruct it from chain data.
findings.recommendation: Make per-row insert failures fatal to the tick so the same block range retries idempotently. In both scan loops, on InsertDiscoveredIntent / HasDepositIntentFor / InsertUnattributedDeposit error, `return err` (or accumulate and return after the loop) instead of `continue`, and only call BumpCursor(toBlock) when no row error occurred. All three inserts are unique-key guarded (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), so re-running the range is safe.

findings.title: deposit_intents unique key omits log_index — second USDC Transfer in one tx is silently dropped
findings.location: packages/db/src/schema/deposits.ts:93 (unique deposit_intents_tx_unique on network,tx_hash); scanner.go 237-266; store.go 112-125
findings.description: The deposit_intents uniqueness is (network, tx_hash) only — log_index is not part of the key (schema deposits.ts:93). InsertDiscoveredIntent does `ON CONFLICT (network, tx_hash) DO NOTHING` (store.go:118). GetTransfersTo (client.go:210) returns one TransferLog per Transfer log in the range, so a single transaction that emits TWO USDC Transfers to the receive address yields two logs with the same tx_hash and different log_index. The discovery loop inserts the first; the second collides on the unique key and is dropped. Only the first transfer's amount_micro is ever credited. Contrast with unattributed_deposits, which IS keyed on (network, tx_hash, log_index) (deposits.ts:137) precisely to avoid this collision — the credit path lacks the same protection. The Inspect path (scanner.go:109-136) reinforces the bug by picking only the FIRST matching USDC transfer, but Inspect's amount is unused for discovered intents (handleOne credits it.AmountMicro), so the loss originates purely in the discovery dedup.
findings.exploitScenario: A user deposits via a batch/multisend contract (Gnosis Safe MultiSend, an aggregator, or a multicall) that emits two USDC Transfers to the receive address in one tx — say 300 + 200 USDC, both from the user's whitelisted wallet. Discovery creates one intent for 300; the 200 is dropped on ON CONFLICT and is never credited or alerted. The user is short 200 USDC with no surfaced record. Two distinct whitelisted users transferring in one batched tx hit the same loss.
findings.recommendation: Add log_index to the deposit_intents uniqueness ((network, tx_hash, log_index)) and change InsertDiscoveredIntent's ON CONFLICT target to match, mirroring unattributed_deposits. Update the API admin/list queries that key on (network, tx_hash) accordingly. Requires a migration; until then, at minimum log a hard warning + create an unattributed-style alert when GetTransfersTo returns more than one USDC log for the same tx_hash so the operator can credit manually.
findings.verifierEvidence: packages/db/src/schema/deposits.ts:93 `unique("deposit_intents_tx_unique").on(t.network, t.txHash)` — log_index omitted; contrast unattributed_deposits.ts:137 which DOES include log_index. Migration confirms it: packages/db/migrations/0032_usdc_payments.sql:74 `CONSTRAINT deposit_intents_tx_unique UNIQUE (network, tx_hash)`. store.go:113-118 `INSERT INTO deposit_intents (...) ... ON CONFLICT (network, tx_hash) DO NOTHING` — discovery inserts the first log; a second USDC Transfer in the same tx collides and is silently dropped. client.go:210-265 GetTransfersTo emits one TransferLog per Transfer event, so two USDC Transfers to the receive address in one tx yield two logs with the same tx_hash, different log_index. scanner.go:109-136 Inspect() `return`s on the FIRST matching USDC transfer — no summation across logs; processor.go:178/189/224-234 credits exactly that single res.AmountMicro. No compensating control: scanner.go:274-277 Scan 2 (unattributed_deposits) explicitly `continue`s past USDC contracts (`strings.EqualFold(lg.Contract, v.contract)`), so the dropped second USDC transfer is recorded NOWHERE and raises no operator alert.

findings.title: BetBuilder: OBB-validated selectionIds are never bound to the persisted ticket_selections that drive settlement — placement can settle a different leg set than was priced
findings.description: For betType="betbuilder" the placement validates the session by calling obbBetsClient.sessionInfo({ sessionId, selectionIds: req.betBuilder.selectionIds, oddsX10000: req.betBuilder.expectedOddsX10000 }) (service.ts:649-653). The payout multiplier frozen into bet_meta is taken verbatim from the client: oddsX10000 = req.betBuilder.expectedOddsX10000 (service.ts:673) and potentialPayoutMicro = multiplyMicroByOdds(stake, oddsX10000/10000) (service.ts:685). SEPARATELY, the rows persisted to ticket_selections — which alone decide won/lost/void at settlement (BetBuilderPayout reads selections[].Result, payout.go:314-340) — are req.selections (marketId/outcomeId), inserted at service.ts:1036-1047. The ONLY checks linking the two arrays are: array-length equality (service.ts:257 `req.betBuilder.selectionIds.length !== req.selections.length`) and that every req.selections leg is same-match + active. NOTHING verifies that the OBB selectionIds (which Oddin priced and validated) actually describe the same (market, outcome) pairs as req.selections. selectionId has the form `<eventUrn>/<providerMarketId>/<outcomeId>?<spec>` (buildSelectionId in betbuilder/routes.ts:73-83) and is fully parseable, but the placement never parses it nor reconciles it against req.selections.
findings.exploitScenario: Attacker quotes an easy/high-probability same-match builder via POST /betbuilder/match/:id/quote, getting a valid sessionId + selectionIds + high expectedOddsX10000 (OBB prices easy combos with low odds, hard combos with high odds — pick the variant that maximizes the gap). Then POST /bets with betType="betbuilder", betBuilder={that sessionId, those selectionIds, that expectedOddsX10000}, but req.selections pointing at DIFFERENT same-match outcomes the attacker actually believes will win (or simply the most-likely outcomes). SessionInfo validates the (sessionId, selectionIds, odds) tuple — all unchanged from the quote — and returns valid. The ticket is debited and pays out at expectedOddsX10000 if the req.selections outcomes (not the OBB-priced ones) all win. Settlement (BetBuilderPayout) resolves win/loss purely from ticket_selections results and multiplies by bet_meta.oddsX10000. Result: bettor receives odds priced for one leg set on the outcome of a different, more-favourable leg set — systematic overpayment / +EV exploit. Must be fixed before ODDIN_OBB_HOST is set.
findings.recommendation: Before debiting, reconstruct the canonical OBB selectionId for every req.selections leg server-side (reuse buildSelectionId with eventUrn + market.providerMarketId + outcomeId + market.specifiersJson) and assert that the SET of reconstructed ids equals the SET of req.betBuilder.selectionIds (order-independent, after the same canonicalization buildSelectionId already does). Reject with a typed error on any mismatch. This makes the OBB-priced legs and the settled legs provably identical. Do NOT trust the client to keep the two arrays consistent.

findings.title: BetBuilder tickets are cashable through the simple-cashout engine, which mis-prices them and lets a bettor control the cashout value via arbitrary per-leg odds
findings.description: compute() refuses to quote only when input.betType is 'tiple' or 'tippot' (algorithm.ts:100-102). 'betbuilder' falls through to the simple-cashout math: ticketOdds = Π(leg.oddsAtPlacement) and offer = stake × ticketOdds × Π(legProb), capped at potentialPayoutMicro (algorithm.ts:113-211). cashout/service.ts:103-119 passes ticket.betType straight in with no betbuilder guard. Two problems: (1) BetBuilder odds are non-multiplicative (Oddin's correlation model — the whole reason BetBuilderPayout exists and bet-delay skips per-leg drift), so Π(leg.oddsAtPlacement) is not the ticket's value; (2) for betbuilder the per-leg drift gate is intentionally skipped at placement (service.ts:507 `if (!isBetBuilder)`), so the client's req.selections[].odds is persisted to ticket_selections.odds_at_placement verbatim with NO server validation (zod only enforces /^\d+(\.\d+)?$/ in routes.ts:35). The bettor therefore controls every leg's oddsAtPlacement, hence controls ticketOdds, hence can drive the cashout offer up to the potentialPayoutMicro cap regardless of true leg probabilities (Π(legProb) shrinks the offer, but with attacker-chosen huge per-leg odds the product saturates the cap).
findings.exploitScenario: With OBB enabled, attacker places a betbuilder ticket whose req.selections[].odds are set to large values (drift check is skipped, so they pass). Ticket pays at the real (low) OBB session odds, but immediately polling GET /tickets/:id/cashout/quote computes stake × Π(hugeOdds) × Π(legProb) and clamps to potentialPayoutMicro — returning a near-full-payout cashout offer before any leg resolves. The bettor accepts the cashout and walks away with near-maximum payout on a bet that has barely moved, a near-risk-free drain. Even without manipulating odds, betbuilder tickets get a cashout priced on an invalid multiplicative model. Fix before enabling OBB.
findings.recommendation: Add `input.betType === 'betbuilder'` to the bet_type_unsupported guard at algorithm.ts:100 (and/or short-circuit in cashout/service.ts before compute()). BetBuilder has no defined cashout model today; refuse to quote, exactly as tiple/tippot do. Independently, even with the OBB binding fix above, betbuilder per-leg oddsAtPlacement remains informational and must never feed a payout/cashout computation.

findings.title: obb-client never sets a gRPC deadline; a hung SessionInfo holds the bet-placement transaction (and its row locks) open inside POST /bets
findings.location: services/api/src/lib/obb-client.ts:177-189 (withDeadline returns empty Metadata; deadline never wired)
findings.description: ObbConfig.deadlineMs is documented but explicitly not wired (obb-client.ts:125-135, 177-189) — withDeadline() returns empty Metadata and the comment concedes it relies on 'keepalive + the OBB caller's outer request timeout (Fastify 30s)'. But the placement calls obbBetsClient.sessionInfo() at service.ts:649 INSIDE the db.transaction started at service.ts:292, AFTER SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the users row (service.ts:320) and the wallet row (service.ts:332). gRPC keepalive (30s) does not bound a request that connected but never responds; without a per-call deadline a slow/hung Oddin OBB endpoint keeps the gRPC call — and therefore the open Postgres transaction holding FOR UPDATE locks on this user+wallet — alive until something else tears the connection down. Concurrent placements by the same user block; pool exhaustion under load.
findings.exploitScenario: Oddin OBB endpoint degrades (network blip, their incident). Each betbuilder placement opens a tx, locks the user+wallet rows, then blocks in sessionInfo() with no deadline. The user's other placements stall on the row lock; pool connections drain. Not a fund-loss bug, but a self-inflicted availability hole that becomes live the moment ODDIN_OBB_HOST is set.
findings.recommendation: Wire a hard per-call deadline (e.g. 3–5s) on SessionInfo via grpc's options.deadline (the proto-loader signature accepts (req, metadata, options, cb)) or an AbortController/setTimeout wrapper, and ideally perform the OBB SessionInfo call BEFORE opening the placement transaction / acquiring the FOR UPDATE locks, caching the validated result, so a slow Oddin never holds DB row locks. Fail-closed (reject placement) on deadline.
findings.verifierEvidence: obb-client.ts:177-189 — withDeadline() returns `new Metadata()` with no deadline; the source comment itself admits "the deadline is set at call site via `options` we bypass" and "For now: rely on keepalive + connect timeout + the OBB caller's outer request timeout (Fastify routes have 30s default)." No options.deadline, AbortController, or setTimeout is wired on any OBB call (lines 194/206/218 all call withDeadline()). service.ts:292 opens db.transaction; service.ts:320 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on users; service.ts:332 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on wallets; service.ts:647-653 `await obbBetsClient.sessionInfo(...)` runs INSIDE that transaction, holding both row locks for the call's full duration. The cited compensating control does not exist: server.ts:88 `Fastify({...})` uses default options — Fastify's requestTimeout defaults to 0 (no timeout), and even when set it only bounds request-body reads + returns 408; it does not abort an in-flight gRPC await or roll back the tx. No statement_timeout / idle_in_transaction_session_timeout / lock_timeout is configured anywhere in the repo. gRPC keepalive (30s, obb-client.ts:172-174) pings the transport, not the application, so a connected-but-hung server keeps the call alive unbounded. The AbortController+setTimeout pattern exists elsewhere (resend.ts:37-38, widgets.ts:105-106) but was not applied to OBB.
